rows.what the ink shows: A continuous upper hook and lower leftward sweep support 5, followed by a separate rounded dot. The proposed closing parenthesis lies along the torn paper edge; the small surviving dark remnant does not establish its full curved stroke.

After the written u_1, a tall right-curving hooked stroke survives through a thick horizontal cancellation, making a closing parenthesis plausible. Separate comma and ellipsis points, and their total extent, cannot be recovered beneath the crossing stroke.

The raised character has a left descending entry followed by a distinct right arch and descending terminal. Those two stem portions support n, rather than the single upper curve and diagonal of 2; the cancellation crosses the lower portion.

A baseline u with two upright sides is visible at the right. At the left, cancellation crosses a triangular or looped body and a small raised curved mark; the raised mark may be n above Lambda or cancellation residue, while a distinct lower n cannot be securely separated.
One compact a-shaped loop with a short rising right terminal follows Car. The intervening paper is blank enough to exclude separate on letters before it.

The surviving upper stroke descends leftward, turns right and ends in a short low stem, closely matching the earlier cursive 4 on this page. It lacks the paired opposing lobes visible in the same-page 3; cancellation merges with the lower tip.

The small index immediately below the closing norm bars has a bent upper stroke, diagonal return and a short rightward foot. It is visibly curved and footed rather than the single upright stroke of 1.

A clear dot stands above the short descending i stroke, and a separate lower horizontal stroke supplies the final n. A thick horizontal run joins the left side of the dotted i body; its connection does not distinguish an extra preceding n from a long entry stroke of i.

The first dotted i with lowered 1, both inequality turns and the second dotted i are visible. Between the turns is an uncancelled horizontal run at index height, distinct from the summation bar; separate ellipsis points are not established, so that notation is also retained uncertain. The lowered terminal glyph has an upright entry and low rightward foot; the adjacent rho index and heading numeral 2 do not securely distinguish 2 from n.

The compact C/e opening is followed by a descending q, joined u and dotted i; the next word has a low re body, v-shaped turn, another i dot, low en strokes and a tall terminal t. That word ends before the separately cancelled token at the image edge, and its longer body supports revient rather than est.

Two dark cancellation strokes overlap the small low word following revient and run toward the right image boundary. The underlying first loop and final joined strokes cannot distinguish au from un, and the edge prevents verification of any obscured continuation or exact extent.

The parenthesized two-loop 8 and low joined en are followed by l and its apostrophe, the compact joined appl body, a separate i dot and a conspicuous descending q loop. The remaining low uan strokes end in an upright t; this dotted-i/descending-q sequence supports appliquant rather than etendant, and the word finishes before the separate a-with-accent and Lambda expression.

Opening and closing paired norm strokes remain visible around an interior crossed by several heavy rising cancellation strokes. Some low curved letters and wedge-like peaks survive, but the middle letter, indices, complete baseline count and exact internal extent are obscured; the source candidate cannot establish them.

The small superscript above the first right-hand Lambda is an open U-shaped loop with a taller left stroke and no securely separate descending p stem. The left-hand p on the same formula is a filled droplet, so that comparison does not justify resolving this open loop as either p or 0.

The low joined mnemo body has a short detached rising accent above its first e. The rest shows the tall crossed t, low e/c join, tall h, joined n, dotted i, descending q and terminal u/e strokes, supporting the complete accented word.
